summary: Laxmanshastri Joshi (1901–1994) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kevalananda Saraswati from around 1916 to 1923 and served as Director at Prajna Pathashala from approximately 1955 to 1994.

Laxmidhar Behera is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur and the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi, and he taught Jivnesh Sandhan.

Lazăr Șăineanu (1859–1934) was a linguist who earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and University of Leipzig, also studying at the University of Paris. Between 1890 and 1892, he acted for Haşdeu at the University of Bucharest.

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University from circa 1894 to 1898 and at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield from circa 1899 to 1903.

LeRoy Carr Barrett (1877–1960) was an Indologist who studied at Washington and Lee University and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Princeton University, Dartmouth College, and Trinity College.

Leah Judith Zahler specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a PhD from the University of Virginia, where she was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins, and also studied under Harvey B. Aronson, Joe Bransford Wilson, and Geshe Wangyal.

Lee Jonathan Chilton works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tasmania, Macquarie University, the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the University of Sydney, where he served on the AABS Executive in 1998.

Lee Ling Ting works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Adelaide, Peking University, and Harvard University, Ting was a PhD candidate at Harvard (attested 2021) and a postdoctoral fellow at Vassar College in 2024.

Lee Yearley is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and sinology who taught Thomas A. Tweed. He held posts at Stanford University as a professor (attested 1989–1992) and later as emeritus (attested 2026).

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2011, he served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus, at Drew University and as a Research Associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College.

Leendert A. van Daalen (1939–1993) was an Indologist who completed his M.A. and Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Henk Bodewitz. He served as Lecturer of Sanskrit at Utrecht (1966–1992) and worked at Leiden University (1992).

Lei Huang is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2012. In 2022, Huang was appointed Assistant Professor at Capital Normal University.

Lei Rong specializes in Tibetology. Educated at East China Normal University, the University of Oslo, the University of Roehampton, and Charles University, Rong holds a post at Xizang Minzu University.

Leigh Lisker (1918–2006) worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania around 1937–1941, where he subsequently served as an assistant professor from 1948 to 1989.

Lemuel Sadoc specialized in philosophy and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from Goethe University Frankfurt by 1924. Sadoc served as a professor at St. Stephen's College, Delhi, in 1926 and taught languages at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad.

Leo Buschardt (1906–1966) worked in Indology and religious studies. After completing an M.A. at the University of Copenhagen (1925–1935), he worked at the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University library in 1943 and the Royal Danish Library in 1944.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), the Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.

Leo Joachim Frachtenberg (1883–1930) was a linguist who studied at Cornell and Columbia under Franz Boas and A. V. Williams Jackson. He served as a lecturer at Columbia (1910–1912) and an ethnologist at the Bureau of American Ethnology (~1912–1917).

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Taitetsu Unno. He held teaching posts at Brown University, the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.
